newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Lawmakers approve Vietnam's plan to introduce VAT.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers approve Vietnam's plan to introduce VAT.

text.p: Vietnam's National Assembly has passed a bill to replace the complex turnover tax with three rates of value added tax (VAT) from 1999, the official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said on Sunday.
VNA said that more than 80 percent of the legislature's deputies voted for the bill, which is part of a continuing overhaul of the country's taxation system.
Under the VAT legislation, tariffs of five, 10 and 20 percent will be levied on goods and services, but there will be no tax on export goods, goods made under contract for export and export services.
Western tax accountants in Vietnam have welcomed the move, saying it signals a major shift in fiscal policy from direct taxes on income to indirect taxes on consumption.
The National Assembly is also due to consider a bill on business income tax, which will substitute the current law on profit tax, during its current session.
The aim of the new business income tax is to level the playing field for foreign and domestic investors and for state-run enterprises and their competitors in the rapidly growing private sector.
